rationale: The dictionary has no country variable; the survey is Chile's CASEN, so 'CHL' would have to be assigned as a constant.
The interview year comes from fecha_año; the survey reference year could also be set as a constant.
The interview month is recorded directly in fecha_mes.
The region variable holds the first-level administrative division.
zona is coded 1=Urbano and 2=Rural, so it must be recoded to 1=urban and 0=rural.
folio identifies the household (comuna, area, seg, viv, hogar), so it is the household identifier.
o is the person order number within the household, which together with folio identifies the person.
expr is the regional expansion factor, the standard CASEN weight; expc (comunal) is the alternative.
CASEN uses the same expansion factor expr for persons and households.
varunit is the variance cluster (conglomerado), the closest available proxy for the primary sampling unit.
varstrat is the variance stratum, which is the survey's sampling stratum.

pco1 gives relationship to the household head and can be recoded: 1=head, 2/3=spouse, 4-6=child, other family codes=other relative, and non-relative codes=non-relative. Domestic worker codes may be among the truncated categories.
sexo uses 1=Hombre and 2=Mujer, which matches the target codes directly.
edad is the person's age in years.
ecivil recodes to the target: 8=single; 1,2,3=union; 4,5,6=divorced or separated (annulled grouped here); 7=widowed.
r3 asks about belonging to an indigenous people (codes 1-9 indigenous, 10=none). Afro-descendant is not asked, so the answers map to indigenous or other.
The Washington Group-style difficulty items h10a-h10f can be coded as disabled if any has 'a lot of difficulty' or 'cannot do' (codes 3-4).
Migrant status can be derived from foreign nationality (r1a), mother's residence at birth abroad (r1b), or residence abroad 5 years ago (r2). The exact definition is a judgment call.
activ gives the employed/unemployed/inactive classification, and it can be rebuilt from o1-o6 plus age. Persons under 15 or 12 map to below working age.
o15 is the occupational category in the main job: 1=employer, 2=own-account, 3-8=employee (including domestic service and armed forces), 9=unpaid family worker.
Occupation is coded in CIUO-88 at 1 digit (oficio1) and 4 digits (oficio4), which can be regrouped into IDB occupation groups.

Industry of the main job (o22_cod) is coded in CIIU rev.3 at 1 and 4 digits and can be regrouped into the IDB industry groups; rama1_sub/rama4_sub refer to the employer paying the worker (o21) and are the alternative.
o10 gives usual weekly hours worked in the main job, with 999 as missing.
Hours are collected only for the main job (o10); o26 asks whether there is a secondary job but no hours for it are recorded.
o23 gives the number of people working in the business, which can be binned into small/medium/large.
o15 category of employment identifies public-sector employees (code 3 government, 4 public companies, possibly 8 armed forces).
Contract type is derived from o16 (indefinite/fixed term), o17 (written contract) and o12 (permanent, seasonal, occasional nature of the job).
o29 asks about contributions to a pension system last month, with code 7 meaning not contributing.
o28 asks directly about affiliation to a pension system; o29 can supplement it for those who are contributing.

yoprcor is the corrected main-occupation income; it combines the corrected wage income (y0101c) and corrected self-employment cash income (y0701c), and its in-kind components would need to be excluded to get the strictly monetary labor income.
Sum of the in-kind payments (especies) from the main wage job, which are the constructed CASEN income variables y0501-y0512.
Income from the secondary occupation, wage (yosa) and independent (yosi), is constructed in the dataset.

Total monetary labor income would be the corrected labor income (ytrabajocor), which includes in-kind items and past-job income, so it may need adjusting; yoprcor plus the secondary-job income is an alternative.
Non-monetary labor income is the in-kind wage payments plus the independent workers' in-kind income (y0801) and own-consumption of agricultural products (yac2).
Monetary non-labor income is total corrected income minus labor income and imputed rent; or it can be built by summing rents, pensions, transfers, subsidies and remittances.
Contributory pensions are old-age and disability pensions (excluding solidarity basic pensions and APS top-ups), survivor, orphan and other pensions.
Money from relatives outside the household, domestic (yfa1) and from abroad (yfa2), approximates remittances; yfa2 alone is the strict international definition.
The survey provides the household's imputed rent (alquiler imputado), including a corrected version.
The dictionary has only the poverty status classification (pobreza), not the poverty line values themselves.
The extreme poverty line value is not given in the dictionary, only the pobreza classification.
e3 asks whether the person currently attends an educational establishment (1=yes, 2=no), and the derived 'asiste' variable gives the same indicator.
The derived 'esc' variable holds years of schooling; it could otherwise be rebuilt from e6a and e6b.
Administrative dependency (e10 or derived depen) identifies municipal and other public institutions, restricted to people who currently attend (e3).
v20 water origin codes 1-3 are public network, which gives piped water access.
v20 gives the water source (network, well, river, truck), and v21 refines how the water is obtained.
v24 covers electricity availability but not whether electricity is the main lighting source, and no lighting-source question is in the dictionary.
v23 gives the excreta disposal system (WC to sewer, septic tank, latrine, none), and v27b counts bathrooms.
v4 is the predominant floor material of the dwelling.
v2 is the predominant exterior wall material.
v6 is the predominant roof material.
v30a gives the number of bedrooms used by the household (v27a is the dwelling total), so v30a is the better match for household-level sleeping rooms.
The survey only counts bedrooms and bathrooms (v27a/b, v30a/b) and has no total number of rooms, so the target cannot be built without assuming it equals bedrooms plus bathrooms.
v13 gives the household's tenure of the dwelling: codes 1-4 are owned, 5-6 rented, and 10-11 de facto occupation. Cesión and usufruct codes (7-9) need a decision about how to classify them.
Internet access is 1 if the household has any paid connection (fixed broadband, mobile broadband, mobile phone with data plan, or tablet with data plan).
r22 asks about a working mobile phone (prepaid or contract), with codes 1-3 meaning yes and 4 meaning no. It is asked at the person level, so it must be aggregated to the household.
r16d asks whether the household has a computer (PC, netbook, laptop) in use and working.
The household equipment items (r16a-r16e) cover water heater, landline, pay TV, computer and smart TV, and none covers a refrigerator.
r14 says whether any household member owns a working vehicle for work or private use, and r15 gives the count. Vehicles are not limited to cars, so this is only an approximation.
